Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh with a matching frame cap delivers smooth, responsive gameplay that suits Dark Souls III's demanding combat well; medium textures and shadows look great upscaled to 1280x800 via FSR.

profiles.Summary: Dark Souls III runs very well on the Steam Deck, achieving a stable 60 fps at medium-to-high settings with the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU comfortably exceeding the game's minimum requirements. The game is Steam Deck Verified with full controller support and reports a platinum ProtonDB rating, making it one of the better experiences on the device.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended specs (GTX 750 Ti / GTX 970) relative to the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU (roughly GTX 1050 Ti class), the platinum ProtonDB rating, and Verified status. On first run, check frame pacing in Irithyll of the Boreal Valley or Lothric Castle — if dips occur at Max Performance, drop to the Optimal profile.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling keeps GPU load minimal; 7 W TDP and 800 MHz GPU clock are sufficient for a locked 30 fps in all areas. A good choice for long sessions away from a charger.

KnownIssues: The game's built-in framerate cap is 60 fps; no native unlock is available without mods, so uncapped play is not possible out of the box.
Online multiplayer (invasions, co-op) may require disabling EAC (Easy Anti-Cheat) workarounds or using specific Proton versions — online play may not function reliably.
Occasional stutters reported in large open areas (e.g., Irithyll of the Boreal Valley) due to asset streaming.
The game defaults to a windowed or incorrect resolution on first launch; manual resolution selection in-game settings is recommended.

MaxPerformance.Notes: The Deck's GPU can handle native 1280x800 at high settings for most areas, though demanding zones like Irithyll may dip to the low 50s; keeping Motion Blur off avoids unnecessary GPU cost with no gameplay benefit.

Optimal.Notes: A 45 fps cap at 90 Hz gives a smooth, responsive feel well-suited to the game's demanding combat; medium textures and shadows look good without overloading the GPU. FSR from 1024x640 keeps the image clean on the OLED screen.

profiles.Summary: Dark Souls III runs well on the Steam Deck OLED, achieving a stable 60 fps at medium settings thanks to its modest PC requirements and the RDNA 2 GPU comfortably exceeding the minimum spec. The game is Steam Deck Verified with full controller support and a platinum ProtonDB rating, indicating a smooth out-of-the-box experience.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements and Steam Deck hardware capability. On first run, check frame rate in a busy outdoor area like the High Wall of Lothric and drop to Optimal or Max Battery settings if you see sustained dips below your target.

MaxBattery.Notes: A rock-solid 30 fps lock with a 7 W TDP and underclocked GPU keeps thermals and power draw minimal; FSR upscaling from 960x600 recovers most visual sharpness. Disable Motion Blur and Depth of Field to reduce GPU load without impacting gameplay.

KnownIssues: The game's built-in frame rate is capped at 60 fps; use the Deck overlay cap to match your target.
Online multiplayer (invasions, co-op) requires an active internet connection and may be affected by anti-cheat compatibility — offline mode is safest for uninterrupted play.
Some players report occasional stutters when entering new areas due to shader compilation on first launch under Proton.
The game defaults to 1920x1080 and must be manually set to 1280x800 or lower in the display settings.

MaxPerformance.Notes: At native 1280x800 with high settings the RDNA 2 GPU can sustain close to 60 fps in most areas, though some dense outdoor zones may dip to the low 50s. Motion Blur is left off to keep the image clean during fast camera movement.
